Owns raw scratch storage without constructing T elements. Preserving growth assigns the overlapping prefix and releases the old run. The source leaves ordinary copy operations implicit and therefore shallow; this review does not invent deep copying or prove any retail copy call.

Aliases the terminal node owned by the list chain; the list deletes it once through first after draining the other nodes.

Registration receives its allocated uppercase extension string. Explicit removal releases it before erasing the node. List destruction deletes nodes without freeing remaining extension strings; preserve that retail leak.
Borrowed typed plugin pointer; finding/removing and virtual getTypeName use the matching list kind. Removing a registration does not destroy the plugin.
